title: Smooth purity
statement:
In the purity conventions of [def-pur-conventions], work at the finite
coefficient stage $\Lambda=A=A_{E,n}$, $n\geq1$. Let $X,Y$ be finite-type $k$-schemes, in the domain of
[def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], and let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth
separated of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$
[def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$, on the
small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], with the derived
operations of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and the twists of
[def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Substituting the diagonal/DNC identification underlying
[thm-pur-diagonal-dualizing-object] (constructed below on this full
finite-type domain) into the tensor formula of
[thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness] gives the canonical isomorphism

$$
\gamma_{f,K}:Lf^*K(d)[2d]\;\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\;Rf^!K
$$

specified by [def-pur-smooth-purity-map]. Its Tate twist, shift, and
trace normalization are fixed by the prescribed Kummer normalization;
the trace is the counit composite of [def-pur-smooth-trace]. The
identification is compatible with arbitrary base change within this
scheme domain, through the smooth pullback exchange of
[def-pur-smooth-pullback-exchange], and with composition of smooth
separated morphisms. Separatedness and finite type have the meanings
collected in [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties].

proof.text:
Put $M=Lf^*K$ and $T=\Lambda_X(d)$. By [def-coefficient-twists-detailed],
$M(d)[2d]=(M\otimes^L T)[2d]$. Compute the tensor using a K-flat
representative $P\to M$ as in [def-weil-derived-tensor]. The degree-$r$
terms of both $(P\otimes T)[2d]$ and $P\otimes T[2d]$ are
$P^{r+2d}\otimes T$; their differential is $d_P\otimes1$ on both sides,
since $T$ is in degree zero and $(-1)^{2d}=1$. These are the total-tensor
and shift conventions of [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] and
[def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. The identity on these terms thus
gives the canonical reassociation
$a_M:M(d)[2d]\xrightarrow{\sim}M\otimes^L T[2d]$.
The calculation is functorial in $P$ and $T$, so is the displayed
identification on derived objects, with no extra scalar or sign.

proof.text:
Set $W=X\times_YX$, with projections $p_1,p_2$, and diagonal $\Delta$. By [lem-pur-diagonal-base-change], $C(p_1,\Delta)\cong\omega_f$. By [lem-pod-separated-finite-type-base-change] and [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence], $p_1$ is separated finite type and smooth of relative dimension $d$. Thus $W$ is finite type over $k$: generators for a composite of finitely generated algebras are the union of the generators at its two stages. By [lem-pur-diagonal-regular-immersion], $\Delta$ is closed with normal bundle $N=T_{X/Y}$. By [lem-sc-smooth-omega-finite-locally-free], $\Omega^1_{X/Y}$ is locally free of rank $d$; its dual has the dual basis on every frame, so $N$ is a rank-$d$ vector bundle, including $d=0$.

The current [thm-pur-dnc-invariance] requires absolutely separated schemes, so apply it locally, not to $W\to X$. A field is Noetherian because its only ideals are zero and the unit ideal; hence $X$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. Choose a finite affine open cover $\{U_i\}$ of $X$. Every open in a Noetherian scheme is Noetherian and quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-open-subscheme-noetherian]; in particular the inverse image of $U_i$ in every affine open of $X$ is quasi-compact. Thus $U_i\hookrightarrow X$ is quasi-compact and finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-qc-open-immersion-finite-type], and $U_i$ is finite type over $k$. Its structure morphism is separated: on an affine its diagonal is induced by the surjection $R\otimes_kR\to R$. Put $W_i=p_1^{-1}U_i$ and $g_i:W_i\to U_i$, with closed section $s_i=\Delta|_{U_i}$. Relative separatedness and finite type follow by base change, and [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](e) makes $W_i$ separated over $k$, since $U_i$ is. Thus both schemes satisfy the actual DNC hypotheses. Restriction of the ideal/conormal description identifies its normal bundle with $N_i=N|_{U_i}$, with zero section $z_i$. Base change for the cohomologically smooth $p_1$ [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness], followed by $Ls_i^*$, identifies $C(g_i,s_i)$ with $\omega_f|_{U_i}$. The current DNC theorem gives
$$\delta_i:\omega_f|_{U_i}\cong C(g_i,s_i)\xrightarrow{\sim}C(\pi_{N_i},z_i).$$
The overlap $U_{ij}=U_i\cap U_j$ is a Noetherian open in the affine $U_i$, hence finite type and separated over $k$ by the same arguments. Its inverse image in $W_i$ is separated finite type as well. The arbitrary-base-change clause of the DNC theorem therefore applies to both inclusions $U_{ij}\to U_i,U_j$ and identifies the restrictions of $\delta_i,\delta_j$ with the same normalized DNC map on $U_{ij}$. No absolute separatedness of $X$ or $Y$ has been assumed. Section invariants here are precisely those of [def-pur-section-invariant].

proof.text:
On every $U_i$, apply [thm-amb-vector-bundle-purity] to $\pi_i:N_i\to U_i$ on the ordinary etale site. The Noetherian hypothesis was checked in Step 2. For $K=A_{U_i}$, its integration-adjoint map $\eta_i^e:A_{N_i}(d)[2d]\to\pi_i^{\times,e}A_{U_i}$ is an isomorphism. By [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison], its comparison pullback is the actual normalized map $\eta_i^p:A_{N_i}(d)[2d]\to R\pi_i^!A_{U_i}$, for every $n\geq1$. A functor preserves inverse equations, so this map is invertible. Its inverse is the specified orientation of [cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity]. Pull back by $z_i$ and use the twist-pullback comparison of the new lemma to form
$$\theta_i:\omega_f|_{U_i}\xrightarrow{\delta_i}C(\pi_i,z_i)\xrightarrow{Lz_i^*(\eta_i^p)^{-1}}Lz_i^*A_{N_i}(d)[2d]\cong A_{U_i}(d)[2d].$$
The restrictions of these maps agree on $U_{ij}$: Step 2 gives agreement of the DNC factor, and the base-change clause of [cor-pur-vector-bundle-purity] gives agreement of its specified inverse vector orientation; the twist-pullback maps commute with restriction by the new comparison lemma.

Here is the gluing argument. Exact open restriction [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] commutes with kernels, images and quotients, hence with the cohomology sheaves [def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Each $\theta_i$ shows that $\mathcal H^r(\omega_f)|_{U_i}=0$ for $r\ne-2d$. The sheaf uniqueness axiom on this cover gives $\mathcal H^r(\omega_f)=0$ for those $r$. Set $F=\mathcal H^{-2d}(\omega_f)$. The good-truncation formulas [def-kun-truncations] give the functorial zigzag
$$\omega_f\ \longleftarrow\ \tau_{\le-2d}\omega_f\ \longrightarrow\ F[2d],$$
whose two arrows induce isomorphisms on every cohomology sheaf and hence are inverted in the derived category. It commutes with the exact restrictions. Under this zigzag and after cancelling $[2d]$, [lem-weil-pbc-derived-single-fully-faithful] identifies each $\theta_i$ with a unique sheaf isomorphism $F|_{U_i}\to A_{U_i}(d)$; their overlap equality gives equality of these sheaf maps. By [lem-pur-sheaf-hom-cover-gluing] the sheaf maps and their inverses glue. Their composites are identities because they are so on every cover member. Composing the resulting sheaf isomorphism with the zigzag gives
$$\theta_f:\omega_f\xrightarrow{\sim}A_X(d)[2d],$$
with restriction exactly $\theta_i$. This is the diagonal/DNC orientation, and it equals the construction of the diagonal theorem on that theorem's restricted domain. This construction glues only morphisms of sheaves in one common degree; it makes no assertion of descent for arbitrary derived morphisms.

proof.text:
Put $M=Lf^*K$. The canonical tensor map $\phi_{f,K}:M\otimes_A^L\omega_f\to Rf^!K$ is an isomorphism by [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness], since $f$ is smooth separated of pure relative dimension $d$ and $K$ is bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude. Form
$$\gamma_{f,K}=\phi_{f,K}\circ(1_M\otimes\theta_f^{-1})\circ a_M.$$
Here $a_M$ is Step 1 and $\theta_f$ is Steps 2–3. Tensoring $\theta_f$ and its inverse preserves their inverse equations; therefore all three arrows and their composite are invertible. This is the specified three-arrow smooth purity map of [def-pur-smooth-purity-map], with the diagonal/DNC orientation just constructed, not a choice from existence of an isomorphism.

source.place: Original corollary Proof, the three-arrow composite

proof.text:
The normalization of the normal-bundle endpoint in Step 3 is fixed at every $n$: choose any $r$ killing $A$, rather than the restricted affine-line datum. In the etale projective-line construction [def-amb-p1-trace] gives $h^e=b^e\iota_2$ and $t^e=\operatorname{pr}_2(b^e)^{-1}$. The map comparison [lem-pur-vector-integration-site-comparison] explicitly gives $\beta_q C(b^e)=b^p$ and $t^p\beta_q=C(t^e)$, identifies restriction by $j_!$, and identifies the projection formula and adjunction transposes defining vector-bundle integration. Consequently $t^ph^p=\operatorname{pr}_2\iota_2=1$ for the prescribed pro-etale Kummer class, and the map $\eta^p$ used in Step 3 is the adjoint of this actual normalized integration. This also covers ramified coefficients without $e\mid n$. Each local DNC arrow in Step 2 is the unique arrow with identity normalization on the standard section invariant, by [thm-pur-dnc-invariance]. Step 3 glues exactly these local orientations by uniqueness for sheaf maps; this introduces no scalar freedom. Thus the orientation $\theta_f$ uses exactly the fixed Kummer-normalized endpoint, the twist $d$ and shift $2d$, and Step 1 introduces no extra sign. The tensor map in Step 4 is specified, not chosen. Finally [def-pur-smooth-trace] supplies the actual counit formula
$$\operatorname{Tr}^{\mathrm{sm}}_{f,K}=\epsilon_{f,K}\circ Rf_!(\gamma_{f,K}).$$
Hence the fixed purity map fixes its trace. We do not infer a trace-map comparison from a comparison of a supported Cartier class; the needed trace, projection and transpose equalities are the separately stated comparison lemma. We do not use the affine-line definition or its model-agreement lemma outside their $e\mid n$ datum.

proof.text:
For a Cartesian square with $f'$ the base change of $f$ and bottom
map $v:Y'\to Y$, put $e=Lu^*\gamma_{f,K}$,
$e'=\gamma_{f',Lv^*K}$, and let $b$ be the canonical pullback-and-twist
identification from the source of $e$ to the source of $e'$. By the
explicit statement of [def-pur-smooth-pullback-exchange],
$\operatorname{Ex}^{!,\mathrm{sm}}=e'\circ b\circ e^{-1}$.
Consequently
$$
\operatorname{Ex}^{!,\mathrm{sm}}\circ Lu^*\gamma_{f,K}
=e'\circ b\circ e^{-1}\circ e=e'\circ b,
$$
which is precisely the square of [thm-pur-smooth-base-change-coherence].
The latter statement applies to arbitrary $v$ between the finite-type
schemes here, with no flatness, smoothness or etaleness condition on
$v$. This is compatibility for the chapter's defined smooth exchange;
it makes no identification with a different right-adjoint mate.

proof.text:
Let $g:Y\to Z$ also be smooth separated of pure relative dimension
$e$, with $Z$ in the same scheme domain, and let $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,\Lambda)$.
The maps constructed in Step 4 are the smooth purity maps to which
[thm-pur-composition-coherence] applies. Its displayed identity is
$$
\gamma_{gf,K}
=c_{g,f}^{-1}\circ\gamma_{f,Rg^!K}\circ
Lf^*(\gamma_{g,K})(d)[2d],
$$
under its canonical identification of the source with
$L(gf)^*K(d+e)[2d+2e]$. This proves composition compatibility for the
specified maps, with the order of exceptional pullbacks fixed by
$c_{g,f}:R(gf)^!\cong Rf^!Rg^!$. In particular the twists add as $d+e$
and the even shifts add as $2d+2e$; no inference from mere existence of
isomorphisms, or from tensor invertibility alone, is used.

Smooth purity: the canonical exceptional inverse image of a bounded constructible finite Tor complex along a smooth separated morphism is its derived pullback with Tate twist d and cohomological shift 2d, compatibly with base change and composition
